Set up a study's environment

Source: R/setup.R
setup.Rd

The one command a study needs before analysis. In order: checks R, installs renv if it is missing, and turns off RStudio's .RData restore and save (a preference for the user, not the study; see workspace_prefs); runs hvtiRutilities::study_setup() with renv on, which cleans up template copies before renv when adopting; declares hvtiR, every member, the packages they need and the team's standard analysis packages in the study's DESCRIPTION; installs them into the study's library with pak and renv; snapshots; checks that every package's dependencies resolve there; and restarts into the project.

Usage

setup(
  study,
  study_tracker_id = NULL,
  root = NULL,
  adopt = FALSE,
  upgrade = TRUE,
  workspace_prefs = TRUE,
  ...,
  derived_from = NULL
)

Arguments

study

The Study Tracker title.

study_tracker_id

The Study Tracker ID, an integer. Give this or derived_from, not both.

root

The study root, where setup() writes. By default the study enclosing the working directory; with none, the RStudio project folder the session is in, once its adoption is confirmed. Outside both, setup() stops and asks for it, so a new study always names its directory.

adopt

Set up an existing study, adding only what is missing. Adopting cleans up template copies unless cleanup = FALSE is passed.

upgrade

Whether the install may move versions the lockfile pins. The default, TRUE, moves them when the declared family needs newer ones: the guard lists each move (package, old and new version, RemoteSha changes) and the snapshot records the new versions. Pass FALSE for a study in revision, whose versions must not move: a locked package the install would move then stops the run and renv.lock is left unchanged.

workspace_prefs

Whether to rewrite the user's RStudio preferences so that .RData is neither restored nor saved. The default, TRUE, applies to every project that user opens. FALSE leaves them as they are.

...

Passed to hvtiRutilities::study_setup(), such as cleanup, template_dir or owner. renv is not accepted: setup() always uses renv, so use hvtiRutilities::study_setup() directly for a study without it.

derived_from

For an exploration of a registered study with no Study Tracker record of its own, the parent's Study Tracker ID. The study gets a provisional ID and checkpoints locally until hvtiRutilities::study_promote() gives it its own.

Value

The study status from hvtiRutilities::study_setup(), invisibly, with attributes healed and missing: data frames of the pins moved and the packages left out.

Details

The usual start is a legacy study opened as its own RStudio project (File > New Project > Existing Directory): run setup(study, study_tracker_id) in that project's console. With no _study.yml there, setup() asks whether to adopt the project folder (the default answer is No), and adopting cleans up template copies unless cleanup = FALSE is passed. It refuses a project opened at one of a study's folders, such as 30_analyses, or at a package. A non-interactive session never adopts unasked: it stops and prints the setup(root = ..., adopt = TRUE) call to run. The step-by-step flow, with where to type each command, is in vignette("start-here").

renv runs in explicit mode: the lockfile records what the study's DESCRIPTION declares, not whatever the code happens to mention. A study that already has a renv.lock keeps its locked versions, and on first conversion every package that lockfile recorded is declared, so none drop out. They are restored, and only packages the lockfile lacks are installed; one the library already holds is kept as it is, unless it is a member. By default (upgrade = TRUE) it moves locked versions the declared family needs and says which; upgrade = FALSE keeps a study in revision on its locked versions.

The standard analysis packages are tidyverse, haven, gtsummary, flextable, survival, survminer, randomForestSRC, varPro and pacman, all from the configured repositories. A study needs no separate step to have them; anything beyond them is added with hvtiRutilities::study_need().

Once the study's renv is active in a session, setup() replaces packages that session has loaded, so rerun it from a session started outside the project, passing root. From inside an active project it stops before installing anything, and names the command to run.

In the install, the study stops using renv's per-user cache (renv::settings$use.cache(FALSE), kept in renv/settings.json, so it applies to everyone), links already in the library are copied in (renv::isolate()), and any link whose target the user cannot read is removed, as is pak's leftover _cache directory, and the package reinstalled. A shared library cannot depend on one user's home.

No personal GitHub token is needed. The family is installed with pak, which carries a shared token, into the study's library, and renv keeps the environment: it restores the lockfile first, then snapshots, and installs from the configured repositories the build-time (LinkingTo) dependencies pak skips. Restoring a package the lockfile pins on GitHub goes through renv, which has no shared token; a GITHUB_PAT (or a token in the git credential store) covers that, and setup() warns when there is none.

Two packages can land in this session's library rather than the study's: renv, and hvtiRutilities with the packages it needs, are installed with pak into the first library in base::.libPaths() when they are missing, and hvtiRutilities also when it is older than 1.5.6. setup() runs them from this session, so they must be there before the study's library exists.

When an install fails, setup() heals what it safely can and leaves out what it cannot. Before it changes renv.lock it copies the file to renv/renv.lock.before-setup-<time>. A restore that fails is healed in up to 10 rounds: a package that will not build under this R moves to the newest version the study's repositories serve (only with upgrade = TRUE), and a missing dependency is installed first; a dependency that will not install leaves its dependents out. After that, setup() keeps leaving out packages outside the family until the restore succeeds. A package left out stays declared but is dropped from renv.lock. With upgrade = TRUE the install stage then retries it at its current release, and it is locked if it installs; with upgrade = FALSE it is not retried, because that would move a pin. A package still missing at the end is named in a warning and recorded in renv/hvtiR-setup.dcf; setup() finishes and opens the project, and doctor() lists what was left out. A package whose dependency is missing stays locked but cannot load until the dependency installs. A family member that cannot install still stops setup(). Each failure's log is kept in renv/logs/.

Safe to rerun: each step checks before it acts.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
setup(
  study = "Study Tracker title", study_tracker_id = 1234L,
  root = "/studies/example"
)
} # }
